- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for sentiment-driven volatility.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and forecasts continued steep rise — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model frequently underestimates mean reversion — add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to capture rebound toward historical mean.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile — increase initial forecast by 0.5–1.0% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to recognize the reversal — delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes (wait 2–3 days) to avoid premature overcorrection.
